newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandans flee threat of rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Ugandans flee threat of rebel attack.

text.p: Hundreds of Ugandans fled a western town after the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces warned it would launch its second attack this week, the independent Monitor newspaper said on Saturday.
Taxis loaded with fleeing residents and their possessions departed Kasese for the two nearest towns of Fort Portal and Mbarara, the newspaper said.
Residents said, despite police appeals to remain calm, they believed the ADF would attack again, following a Tuesday assault which was repulsed.
One military source dismissed the threat: "We gave these fools what they wanted on the 15th (July) and have continued pursuing them up in the mountains."

The ADF, a mainly-Moslem rebel group, has made hit and run attacks on western Uganda villages since up to 100 civilians died and 30,000 fled when they attacked Bundibugyo town from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in June.
